summary:
The compliance review of the CarKey product, which facilitates Used-Car Loans Through Dealers, identified the following findings against the reviewed RBI rules:

1. A high-risk finding was noted under DLD2025:9(i) regarding the loan being paid directly into the dealer's bank account, as this may not align with the requirement for loan disbursement to be made directly to the borrower's account.

2. A low-risk finding was noted under DLD2025:11(ii), where the feature correctly states that nodal grievance officers of both companies are named on both websites, in the app, and in the KFS, complying with the requirement to prominently display contact details of the nodal grievance redressal officers.

3. A high-risk finding was noted under DLD2025:26(ii), as the product feature does not specify the validity period of the DLG agreement in relation to the longest tenor of the loan, which is up to 6 years. The DLG agreement must remain in force for at least the longest tenor of the loan.

No other gaps were found against the reviewed RBI rules.
